q: Which material has the greatest mass for its size?
How many times heavier is 1 cm3 of water than 1 cm3 of air?
Use the data to describe the pattern between state and density.
Solids are usually densest (gold, iron), liquids a little less, and gases far less dense (air); but ice is an exception: less dense than liquid water.
Ice floats on water. Use the data and particles to suggest why this is unusual.

Ice (0.92) is less dense than water (1.00), so it floats. Usually particles are closer in a solid; in ice the water particles are held in an open pattern with more space, so ice takes up more room than the same mass of water.
